newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa continues charity work in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa continues charity work in hospital.

text.p: Mother Teresa, in stable condition as she recovers in hospital from heart surgery, continued her charity work to help the poor from her sickbed, her doctors said on Saturday.

"She asked a lady, wife of a patient at the hospital, if she could get old sarees from her for the poor. This morning the lady came with almost 100 sarees, 50 new, for weddings of the poor and 50 old sarees," they said in a regular medical update.
"Mother was so happy and immediately sent the sarees with the Sisters to Missionaries of Charity," added the update, issued by Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre.
The bulletin, at noon (0630 GMT), said the revered nun was cheerful and had breakfast sitting on a chair, but needed care and monitoring to keep her stable.
Indian Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav visited Mother Teresa on Saturday, accompanied by a government minister of the state of West Bengal, where Calcutta is located, it added.
An earlier bulletin said she was improving and had said her morning prayers seated in a chair, but was not out of danger.
Though seriously ill, the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her work with the poor and the destitute, has been asking doctors to let her go home.
Mother Teresa, known by many as the "Saint of the Gutters", had heart surgery, for the third time in five years, to clear two blocked coronary arteries on November 29.
Her recovery was delayed by an irregular heartbeat and long-standing lung and kidney trouble.

"Mother Teresa remains the same as yesterday (Friday) afternoon," the bulletin said. "Lung congestion has mildly improved. Bronchitis persists. Pneumonia showed some improvement but not totally cleared. Cardiovascular status stabilising."
"She has had a good sleep last night, but continous care and monitoring is needed in order to keep her stable," it added.
Mother Teresa's doctors have cautioned that her recovery will be slow and she might never be as active as before.
Doctors said on Wednesday they successfully regulated her heartbeat with a mild electric shock, but persistent bronchitis continued to hamper her recovery.
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda plans to visit Mother Teresa on Tuesday, state government officials in Calcutta said.
